parts: Please read /papers/investigations-5/04_three_regime_heat_flow_dynamics/notes/06_CHAT0001_RESEARCH_SUMMARY_20261027.md, review the research overview and progress file, and describe the status of the project at a high level.
I’ll read the research summary, overview, and progress file, then describe the main results, open questions, and current direction.

The main advance is a stronger bound on where a nonreal zero can be found near time zero. It remains compatible with all three regimes. The response-analysis branch has also identified why one proposed method fails as the observation window grows.

As of **27 October 2026**, the investigation has obtained substantive quantitative analytical results, but **has not yet distinguished which of the three regimes the canonical heat flow occupies**. RH, simplicity, and exclusion of a positive Newman threshold remain open.

The [research overview](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/04_three_regime_heat_flow_dynamics/research-overview/01_THREE_REGIME_DYNAMICS_RESEARCH_OVERVIEW_20261026.md) compares three possibilities:

| Regime | Meaning | Expected behavior just before time zero |
|---|---|---|
| A | RH fails; Newman threshold is positive | Nonreal zeros persist in a bounded region. |
| B | RH holds, with some multiple zeros | Multiple zeros split into nearby nonreal zeros. |
| C | RH holds, with all zeros simple | Nonreal zeros leave every fixed bounded region as time approaches zero. |

The strongest recent advance is the [summary’s quantitative bound](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/04_three_regime_heat_flow_dynamics/notes/06_CHAT0001_RESEARCH_SUMMARY_20261027.md):
\[
R_*(\tau)\le \exp\!\exp\!\left(C_d/\sqrt{\tau}\right),
\qquad 0<\tau\le1,
\]
where \(R_*(\tau)\) is the distance from the origin to the nearest nonreal zero at time \(-\tau\). This improves the earlier double-exponential bound with \(\tau^{-3}\) in the inner exponent. The gain comes from constructing much more tightly localized seed zeros and carrying their estimates through the full approximation and transport argument.

Its significance is a stronger guarantee that a nonreal zero exists within a specified radius. **It supplies neither a lower escape rate nor the actual first-zero location**, and all three regimes satisfy it. The constants also remain unevaluated, so there is no practical numerical location bound yet.

The other main branch studies how an observable detects multiple zeros. It now has an explicit fixed-window response with an \(O(\tau^2)\) remainder and estimates for observation error. Extending this to expanding windows remains unresolved. A separate continuation established that one specified global error-budget method fails for the tested growing-window scales; localized alternatives remain available.

The [progress register](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/papers/investigations-5/04_three_regime_heat_flow_dynamics/research-progress/01_THREE_REGIME_DYNAMICS_RESEARCH_PROGRESS_20261026.md) therefore appropriately marks the quantitative tasks **Partial**. Connecting these results to the full physical equations, excluding a positive threshold, and obtaining an estimate that rules out a regime remain **Open**.

The clearest next steps are to reduce the costly recurrence estimate in the Dobner construction, or certify a concrete seed contour and evaluate the missing constants on a specified interval. The response branch needs a localized estimate that remains effective as the window grows. The larger scientific objective is an independently established constraint from the canonical source that conflicts with one regime’s required behavior.

These results currently have analytical proofs recorded in notes and internal same-model reviews, with no numerical certification or independent specialist review—consistent with the repository’s [status conventions](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/result-summaries/README.md) and [review limitations](/Users/ebbaker/Documents/shifted-zeta-positivity/avoid/05_same_model_reviews_and_shared_premises.md).
